correctness.rationale: Let M be point/block incidence, with r=(v−1)/(k−1), b=vr/k. Point pair uniqueness gives MMᵀ=(r−1)I+J. The Laplacian Schur complement for a dipole from point p0 to incident block B0 is (vI−J)/k. The gauge x=(k/v)e_p0−(1/v)1_B0 and y=(Mᵀx−e_B0)/k satisfy both Kirchhoff equations. The six distinct edge-current types follow from the fact that distinct blocks intersect in at most one point; their count gives total |current| R+5(k−1)(v−k)/(vk)=5−4/k−4(k−1)/v, with diagonal R=1/k+(k−1)/v∈(0,1). Thus the complementary P=I−Q absolute column sum is 1+||Q_col||_1−2R=6−6/k−6(k−1)/v. Every incidence is arbitrary, and Q/P symmetric, giving both endpoint norms. k=2 boundary and strict dominance sign (k−2)v>2k(k−1) are correct. Independent standard-library rational checking verified all 167 individual source-incidence current and complement column sums over five design realizations, including Fano, AG(2,3) and a cyclic STS(13); the quantifiers are proved analytically, not extrapolated from finite cases.

value.rationale: Steiner 2-design incidence graphs form a natural infinite family including nonsymmetric systems; exact endpoint norms of canonical electrical cut/cycle projectors are directly relevant to graph transportation and Banach projection geometry. The universal dependence only on (v,k), not on incidence symmetries, and the sharp Q/P dominance change at (k−2)v=2k(k−1) provide motivated exact invariants. This is not a textbook substitution or known-table value; no minimality among all projections is asserted.

final_claim: For every existing Steiner 2-(v,k,1) design, 2≤k<v, the real unit-edge incidence-graph canonical Euclidean orthogonal cut projection Q has exact ℓ1 and ℓ∞ norm 5−4/k−4(k−1)/v; its cycle complement P has norm 6−6/k−6(k−1)/v; every source-edge column attains its corresponding sum. Cycle dominates iff (k−2)v>2k(k−1), with the equality boundary included.
limitations: Only existing Steiner designs; no existence result, weighted extension, intermediate ℓp norm, or minimality among arbitrary projections.
Possible unindexed stronger Steiner electrical network result could cover the exact norm; primary and semantic searches do not certify priority.
Five finite design checks corroborate but do not entail the infinite identity.
